[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
The Edinburgh proclamation of 6 February 1794 names Elisabeth Glasgow, widow of John Williamson, a miner of Carnwath, and Alexander Thomson, a travelling merchant. Both parties were in New Greyfriars parish. The Ancestry index gives the bride as Elisabeth Glasgow or Williamson.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso40scotuoft/page/781/mode/2up Francis J. Grant, ed., Register of Marriages of the City of Edinburgh, 1751–1800, p. 781].</ref><ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60144/records/3184080 Scotland, Select Marriages, 1561-1910 — , 6 Feb 1794, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The register gives the date of proclamation. No birth date or parents are named. Bessie Glasgow, baptised at Covington and Thankerton in 1750 to George Glasgow and Agnes Williamson, is a geographically plausible namesake; no record links that child to either marriage.
